cards.defeat: Reject the proposed perception mechanism if disclosure demonstrably raises perceived effort yet later frequency and request size remain unchanged. Unequal physical service confounds the comparison; failure to change perception makes a null result inconclusive. Any missed correct seal defeats the present action.
cards.mutation: Invert the hypothesized return link by associating apparently inexpensive trolley deliveries with their occupied transfer minutes, while preserving initial demand and physical service. This is a proposed later communication intervention, not an observed effect or an extra present operation control.
cards.prediction_candidate: Tool-induced later-demand hypothesis: conditional on higher perceived service cost, effort disclosure produces fewer later requests and larger quantities per request than the sham, at equal total later requirements.
cards.prediction_rival: Exogenous later-demand hypothesis: later requirements determine requests independently of perceived trolley cost, so effort disclosure and sham produce unchanged frequency and size.
